item.title: 'Worst aquarium ever' review sends whaling museum's sales soaring 250%
item.description: The New Bedford Whaling Museum in Massachusetts turned a one-star Google review that called it the "worst aquarium ever" into viral merchandise that is flying off shelves.
item.content:encoded:
A museum is cashing in after a one-star Google review calling it the "worst aquarium ever" became an unexpected viral hit.

The New Bedford Whaling Museum in Massachusetts, which highlights the history, science and art of whaling rather than marine animals, embraced the one-star review by boldly printing the phrase on T-shirts, sweatshirts and tote bags.

The merchandise has since gone viral on social media — sending sales soaring by 250% in just one week, The Associated Press (AP) reported.

MYSTERY OF GOLD COIN SHIPWRECK FINALLY UNMASKED AFTER 30 YEARS: 'FANTASTIC CONCLUSION'

The now-famous review was posted on Google in 2020 after a visitor mistakenly referred to the museum as an aquarium, writing that it was "the worst aquarium ever."

Rather than ignore the criticism, staff turned it into a merchandise design last fall, featuring the review on the back and a whale skeleton on the front.

The shirts have recently gained national attention after they were featured in multiple news outlets, helping to introduce the museum to an even wider audience.

"They took a chance on something, and it obviously hit," Amanda McMullen, president and CEO of the museum, told the AP.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Adding to the irony, the museum opened a 250-gallon saltwater tank earlier this year featuring local marine life, including blue crabs, sea stars and northern puffer fish, as part of a partnership with the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth's School for Marine Science and Technology.

The unexpected success reflects the institution's personality, said Annelise Conway, chief engagement officer at the Whaling Museum. 

"There isn't a strategy to be authentic," Conway told the AP. "It just sort of happens."

"The person who sold you your ticket is the person who is modeling the merchandise," Conway added.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

The museum's decision to embrace the joke has also won over social media users, who praised it for turning the review into a marketing success.

"I love it. Kudos to the museum for leaning into the joke and embracing it," one Reddit user wrote.

Another commenter joked, "I think it takes courage to walk into a museum with the word 'Whaling' in the name and think, 'I bet there's a dolphin show.'"

Others said the museum deserves the newfound attention.

"It's honestly a great museum," a user commented. "I love that it's gone viral because it's just a wonderful place to support."

Fox News Digital reached out to the Whaling Museum for comment.

The Associated Press contributed reporting.

item.title: Florida Gators coach reveals damning clip of ESPN host sniffing a high-heel as foot feud escalates
item.description: Jon Sumrall fired back at Dan Orlovsky's anti-pedicure stance with a devastating photo of the ESPN analyst smelling Molly Qerim's shoe on air.
item.content:encoded:
We're two days away from August, and the college football season is already starting to heat up.

Sort of.

New Florida Gators head coach Jon Sumrall and ESPN football analyst Dan Orlovsky have been going back and forth this week over the most offseason topic of all time: pedicures.

ESPN'S DAN ORLOVSKY WEIGHS IN ON FLORIDA COACH JON SUMRALL'S PEDICURE PREFERENCES, IMMEDIATELY GETS ROASTED

That's right. You read that right. Pedicures.

Sumrall's wife let the cat out of the bag last week that the new UF coach has a secret passion for pedicures, saying that it's his "favorite extra thing to do," and that he gets one "every two weeks during football season."

Relatively harmless interview, and one that, frankly, I didn't think would get much play given the news cycle.

Boy, was I wrong.

Orlovsky hopped on ESPN's 'Get Up' this week, and angered America when he declared that he was "completely against pedicures for dudes."

"You're a dude. You're not supposed to get pedicures. I am so against this. You should not be getting pedicures... I'd rather have awful feet than get pedicures," he continued.

Everyone is entitled to their opinion, and Orlovsky made his stance clear. In turn, Sumrall took to X and stuffed the ESPN analyst in a locker with a photo so damning, I'm not even sure Orlovsky can come back from it:

Goodness gracious.

Hand up, I forgot that picture/video of Dan Orlovsky existed. For those who don't follow ESPN religiously (all of you, I hope), that's a clip from a few years back on 'First Take' when Orlovsky, for some reason, decided to smell host Molly Qerim's shoe live on air.

He just ... smelt it:

My God. What a scene. What a moment for ESPN.

How does Dan Orlovsky, in good faith, make the pedicure comments when he KNOWS that clip is lingering in the ether? If I knew that footage existed, I would never, ever, ever, hop on ESPN and say a single word about feet.

I'd keep my mouth shut, my head down, and my eyes forward, and just pray nobody ever brings it back up.

PS: I don't agree with Orlovsky because I know plenty of dudes who get pedicures (well, just two, but still), but I also don't think it was the dumbest thing I've ever heard someone say. It's locker room talk. Guy speak. Clubhouse banter.

If you're in a locker room and say you get pedicures, you're gonna catch flack, even if the other dudes in there get them, too. That's how we operate.

I have no idea how the Gators are going to be this season. I assume pretty mediocre given the past decade, but maybe I'm wrong.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

I do know that Jon Sumrall is off to a blazing start with this takedown of Dan Orlovsky. We need more of this at UF. Things have gotten so bland around here.

Not anymore. Not in July, at least.

Now, let's see this energy in October.

item.title: California lifeguard speaks out on heartstopping ocean rescue: 'I love what I do'
item.description: Ryder Williams described fighting volatile waves while holding the limp 10-year-old at Santa Cruz Beach, revealing details of the rescue seen worldwide.
item.content:encoded:
A 16-year-old lifeguard whose daring rescue of a 10-year-old on Saturday went viral finally spoke out about the harrowing save in a Wednesday statement.

Ryder Williams, the teen hero whose daring rescue of a young boy at Santa Cruz Beach on Saturday captivated the nation, described the episode in a statement released by his employer, California State Parks.

"I was at the waterline 15 yards downcoast of Tower 2 making a safety contact when I looked up and saw a child about 20 (yards) up from the tower lose his footing in ankle deep water," the statement opened.

OFF-DUTY ICE OFFICER RELIES ON 'SIXTH SENSE' TO SAVE DROWNING CHILD BEFORE DELIVERING MESSAGE TO CRITICS

"I radioed it in, threw my radio and sunglasses at the base of my tower as I ran toward the kid. I put my fins on my wrist, popped my buoy and entered the water to get ahold of the child. Due to the volatility of the water, I was unable to tube up the victim. After the first wave I was unable to pull him out because he was limp and the waves were pushing so hard. There were two to three more waves before lifeguard Aaron Bohnen entered the water to help me. There were bystanders who jumped in to try to help, and I yelled at them all to get back to shore," Williams' statement continued.

"Once Bohnen and I got the kid to shore I was instructed to get the med bag from Bohnen’s unit and we assessed the child. Shortly after, I got back into my tower where I returned to provide lifeguard services for the rest of my shift," he continued.

‘HERO' MOM DIES AFTER USING LAST STRENGTH TO SAVE 4-YEAR-OLD SON FROM FLORIDA RIVER

"I’m grateful to have had the opportunity to return the child to his family safely. This is my job and I love what I do. I’m thankful to my fellow lifeguards who perform rescues just like this every day," Williams' statement concluded.

Williams' heroics earned him national attention, praise and even an invitation to the White House.

MISSING GRAND CANYON HIKER, 83, RESCUED AFTER GETTING SEPARATED FROM COMPANION

"We’re going to bring this heroic young man, and his family, into the White House with, perhaps, the boy he saved, to give him a High Civilian Honor. Very brave, he deserves it!" the White House wrote in an X post attributed to President Donald Trump.

Williams' rescue was one of 34 rescues in the Santa Cruz district over the weekend, California State Parks said in a statement obtained by FOX 2 KTVU.

"All California State Park lifeguard towers were staffed, there were 6 units on, a two-person rescue water craft team, three permanent lifeguard units, and a lifeguard supervisor working in Pajaro Coast," California State Parks also said of the weekend.

The 10-year-old boy Williams rescued was identified by KTVU as being named Nathaniel. His father, Sumit Rai, praised Williams' efforts in an interview with KTVU.

"It was a remarkable effort to bring him back to shore. I mean Ryder fought the sea," he told the outlet.

"It's really hard to fight that, and my son was unconscious. He weighs about 100 pounds, and he was limp, so that's basically dead weight that he had to carry and hold onto to pull back to shore," he continued.

"It's so easy to let go, and he knew that if he lets go then he's gonna basically just float away, and he's gone. That's the end of it, and he would have died," Rai concluded.

Fox News Digital contacted California State Parks for comment and additional information.

item.title: NFL employees’ troubling driving incidents mount, costing jobs and putting others at risk
item.description: From Tony Romo's OWI arrest to Kyle Shanahan's collision, the NFL has recorded 21 driving incidents since 2024 among its personnel, or about one per month.
item.content:encoded:
Many years ago, before drunk-driving charges were euphemized as driving while intoxicated, Dan Marino liked to imbibe a little. But he also enjoyed getting around South Florida because he was the quarterback of the Miami Dolphins, not a hermit.

Marino understood his stature in the community and what an unacceptable pratfall a drinking and driving charge would be on charges of his reputation. So he bought a limousine. And he hired a driver.

That driver, who happened to be the father of future NFL great and current Carolina Panthers general manager Dan Morgan, would drive Marino everywhere, making sure the star quarterback, who liked a few drinks now and then, never had any issues on the road.

TONY ROMO ARRESTED IN MILWAUKEE FOR ALLEGED OWI OFFENSE: REPORT

The NFL, its players and coaches could definitely use more of Dan Marino's thinking now because events in the past couple of years suggest the league has something of a driving problem.

Consider what has happened this month so far:

VIKINGS SUSPEND ASSISTANT GERALD ALEXANDER AFTER GUILTY DUI PLEA

We are not close to being done.

The Washington Commanders fired tight end coach Ben Steele on the eve of training camp following a DWI arrest in June.

"Certainly really wish the best for Ben and his family," Commanders general manager Adam Peters said this week. "A lot of thought was put into that decision and, you know, it was unfortunate but hoping for the best for him and his family."

Before the draft, OutKick reported that University of Miami defensive lineman Rueben Bain Jr. got into an accident in October 2025 and was cited for reckless driving. That followed a March 2024 fatal accident in which Bain hit another car on I-95 in South Florida, setting off a chain reaction accident that eventually left one of his passengers non-responsive.

That passenger eventually died.

Bain was drafted in the first round by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, but the Top 10 prospect dropped to the No. 15 overall slot.

Kansas City Chiefs receiver Rashee Rice served 30 days in jail from May to June because he tested positive for THC (marijuana) and the reason we know this is because those tests are part of a probation agreement stemming from his well-chronicled driving conviction.

Rice in July 2025 pleaded guilty to third-degree felony charges (collision involving serious bodily injury, and racing on a highway causing bodily injury) following a high-speed March 2024 crash in Dallas.

Fox News Digital compiled records of 21 driving incidents involving NFL people dating back to 2024 that speak to drinking and driving, reckless driving or simply bad decision-making behind the wheel when viewed individually.

But when one understands NFL-connected people – not including their families – are involved in more than one traffic-related mishap per month on average, it could signal a problem.

An NFL spokesman could not be reached for comment on this matter, but a league source told Fox News Digital this is an individual and club matter.

Clubs instruct their employees not to drink and drive, something they probably should already know. Some clubs connect players and others with rideshare programs or tell players to call club security if they feel unsure of their ability to drive.

But a large percentage of these incidents, like Shanahan's head-on collision, do not involve alcohol.

More NFL drivers apparently could learn something from the Dan Marino example.

item.title: Zac Brown Band's John Driskell Hopkins says he's 'chasing the clock' after ALS diagnosis
item.description: John Driskell Hopkins says he's "chasing the clock" since his 2021 ALS diagnosis, still touring with Zac Brown Band while planning for 2027.
item.content:encoded:
Zac Brown Band's John Driskell Hopkins is opting to look at his ALS (amyotrophic lateral sclerosis) diagnosis in a different light and is trying to make everyday count.

Over a decade after the Ice Bucket Challenge surfaced on social media, it is making a comeback. During an interview with Fox News Digital about the challenge, Hopkins explained that after his diagnosis in 2021, he's been "chasing the clock" ever since.

"I'm almost busier now than I was before because I'm trying to get so much done. I'm tryin' to fit it all in. I'm taking more family vacations. I'm in the studio more than I should be. I'm still on tour with Zac Brown Band right now. You know, my fingers work. My voice works, it's been compromised, but most of the set, no one would notice," Hopkins, a founding member of Zac Brown Band, said.

He continued, "And I'm playing different things on stage, but they still don't make sense. You know, I'm chasing the clock more than I ever have been. And what I worry about is that that is causing me stress, which might be exacerbating my condition. So it's a bit of a catch-22, you know, I've created."

ZAC BROWN BAND'S JOHN DRISKELL HOPKINS FIGHTS ALS DIAGNOSIS: ‘CRYING SUCKS’

Acknowledging the reality of his diagnosis, Hopkins said that he's looking toward the future where he might not be able to sing.

"I hope that my progression continues to be slow and that I can sing for a long time, but who knows?" he said.

In 2014, Hopkins and the Zac Brown Band participated in the ALS Ice Bucket Challenge on social media – years before his diagnosis. At the time, Hopkins had no idea what the disease was, let alone that he would be diagnosed one day.

WATCH: Zac Brown Band's John Driskell Hopkins is 'chasing the clock' after ALS diagnosis

"I didn't even know what it was. I mean, I think a lot of people in the band that did the challenge with me understood that it was neurological and fatal, but we didn't have any clue as to how it affected the body more," he began.

"Certainly not how cases were increasing. I mean, we have seen an explosion of neurodegenerative diseases and I can only, generally point to maybe its toxicity. You know, maybe in the world where we're just consuming a lot more things that are doing us harm. That's all I can guess. But I would have never thought… I was indestructible in 2014, you know?"

With several notable public figures recently diagnosed with ALS, the Ice Bucket Challenge has begun resurfacing across social media. Hop and his team at Hop On A Cure have now joined in, sharing their own Ice Bucket Challenge video and passing the challenge on to fellow ALS organizations, as well as the Zac Brown Band.

MICHAEL J. FOX SAYS GOING PUBLIC WITH PARKINSON'S WAS 'HELL' ON WIFE TRACY POLLAN

Hopkins told Fox News Digital he's glad the trend has come back around this summer. Hopkin's nonprofit organization and the Zac Brown Band posted videos on Instagram in July participating in the challenge.

"It's very popular, and it's fun in the summer. It's been a really hot summer this year, all over the world. And we were in London with 95 degree days, and they never see that," Hopkins said.

When asked how he's been able to stay strong during his diagnosis, Hopkins told Fox News Digital that he doesn't feel strong at all.

LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"I don't feel strong, people often ask me where my strength comes from, but I feel incredibly weak, not just physically. You know, I'm an actor, I have a theater degree, so I'm acting strong," he said.

WATCH: John Driskell Hopkins talks about the viral ALS Ice Bucket Challenge

Hopkins was diagnosed with ALS just before Christmas in 2021 and announced his diagnosis in May 2022. After his diagnosis, Hopkins and his wife, Jennifer, founded the nonprofit organization, Hop On A Cure, to help accelerate research to prevent, reverse and ultimately cure ALS while also raising awareness and supporting families affected by the disease.

At the time of his diagnosis, Hopkins emphasized that his disease had been slowly progressing, allowing him to continue touring and performing with the band.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

During his interview with Fox News Digital, Hopkins said he's in a different position than 99% of ALS patients because he is still able to plan for the next calendar year.

"The fact that I still see next year in my future puts me in a different position than 99.9% of ALS patients. The fact that I'm looking to my calendar for '27. I'm gonna be at the 30a Songwriters Festival '27, and maybe I won't be able to sing what I can now, but maybe I will, you know, we just don't know, and I appreciate you recognizing that reaction as strength, but to me, it's getting up every day that I can and doing what I do," Hopkins concluded.

item.title: Captured 'America's Most Wanted' fugitive Ronald Fischer abandons alias after 20 years on the run
item.description: Ronald Fischer lived as "Dr. Richard Graydon" for over 20 years before a tip led U.S. Marshals to his 56-foot sailboat off New Jersey's coast.
item.content:encoded:
After more than 20 years on the run, an "America's Most Wanted" fugitive who disappeared in the middle of his sexual assault trial stood before a Rhode Island judge this week under his real name for the first time since fleeing justice.

Ronald Fischer, 70, identified himself by his real name during a hearing in Newport Superior Court, where a judge canceled an outstanding warrant tied to his alleged failure to appear for trial in April 2005, arraigned him on a bail-jumping charge and set bail at $20,000 surety.

Fischer was arrested earlier this month aboard the 56-foot sailboat "Silver Lining" off the coast of New Jersey after investigators received a credible tip about his whereabouts.

'AMERICA'S MOST WANTED' FUGITIVE CAPTURED ON SAILBOAT OFF NJ COAST AFTER 20 YEARS ON THE RUN

During Monday's hearing, Fischer appeared without an attorney as the court discussed appointing counsel.

His next court appearance is scheduled for Aug. 17.

Authorities said Fischer had been living under the alias "Dr. Richard Graydon" while eluding capture for more than 20 years.

'AMERICA'S MOST WANTED' EX-COP FUGITIVE RETURNED AFTER 20 YEARS ON THE RUN TO FACE MURDER, CHILD SEX CHARGES

Fischer disappeared during his 2005 sexual assault trial in Rhode Island, where he was accused of sexually assaulting a woman aboard his boat at a Portsmouth marina in 2003. He was later convicted in absentia and remained one of the state's most wanted fugitives, appearing multiple times on "America's Most Wanted."

An affidavit previously obtained by Fox News Digital details how investigators believe Fischer meticulously planned his disappearance before vanishing.

Investigators wrote that Fischer emailed his attorney on April 23, 2005, saying he intended to flee the country rather than risk a conviction. Later that evening, they said he called each of his daughters and told them he was leaving the United States.

According to the affidavit, Fischer contacted a New York travel agency before purchasing an American Airlines ticket from Boston to London, only to cancel the reservation before boarding the flight.

Surveillance cameras later captured him returning a rental car to an Enterprise location in Boston shortly after midnight before walking away carrying two travel bags.

Investigators also determined Fischer spent the days before his disappearance putting his affairs in order by transferring vehicles to his daughters, instructing them to remove their belongings from his home and disposing of a Jaguar before vanishing.

SEND US A TIP

The affidavit also alleges Fischer emailed attorney Robert Mann explaining he had decided not to risk being convicted in Rhode Island and instead planned to leave the country to pursue what he described as "a good, safe, secure and comfortable life."

Fischer now faces sentencing in the sexual assault case, a felony bail-jumping charge and a pending federal charge alleging unlawful flight to avoid prosecution.

The U.S. Marshals Service credited a multi-agency investigation and a public tip with leading investigators to Fischer's capture, ending what it described as one of Rhode Island's longest-running fugitive cases.

item.title: Rare pagan masterpiece emerges near where St Paul spread teachings of Christianity
item.description: Depicting the river god Eurymedon, a rare mosaic was found on Theater Street in Aspendos, just miles from where the Apostle Paul spread Christianity.
item.content:encoded:
Excavators recently uncovered an ornate Roman mosaic at an archaeological site in Turkey, near where the Apostle Paul helped spread Christianity beyond the Levant.

The mosaic was found at Aspendos, an ancient city about 25 miles east of Antalya in southern Turkey, the country's Ministry of Culture and Tourism announced in June.

It was discovered on Theater Street in Aspendos, which connects the city's acropolis — or citadel — with its theater.

ARCHAEOLOGISTS UNEARTH ANCIENT TREASURE CACHE AT BIBLICAL CITY CONNECTED TO GENESIS

Aspendos lies just miles from Perga, the biblical city mentioned in Acts 13:13 and 14:25 where the Apostle Paul traveled during his first missionary journey.

Pictures of the mosaic show a depiction of the youthful river god Eurymedon, framed by geometric patterns and aquatic imagery.

Officials said the god is "depicted holding and wearing reed leaves."

1,740-YEAR-OLD ROMAN COIN BEARING EMPEROR'S NAME FOUND AS ENGLAND RAIL DIG REVEALS CLUES

"He leans against an amphora from which water flows, symbolizing nature's abundance and the life-giving power of water," the translated statement said.

Archaeologists believe the pagan mosaic once formed the floor of a pool built in the early 3rd century A.D.

The mosaic floor covers roughly 20 by 25 feet and "is believed to continue into areas that have not yet been excavated," officials said.

"Researchers believe the structure was subdivided into separate rooms following the 262 A.D. earthquake."

ANCIENT ESTATE TIED TO GROUP IN THE BIBLE UNEARTHED WITH 'FASCINATING' TREASURES IN ISRAEL

Depictions of the river god Eurymedon are exceptionally unusual in ancient mosaics, according to Turkish officials. 

The god is "represented by only a limited number of known examples," said the statement.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Mehmet Nuri Ersoy, the Turkish minister of culture and tourism, noted that the mosaic was of "great scientific importance."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"It is also especially significant because depictions of river gods are extremely rare in mosaic art," Ersoy said in the release.

"This discovery not only reveals the artistic richness of Aspendos, but also provides important scientific data on Roman-period Anatolian mosaic art."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

The discovery is one of many archaeological finds in Turkey, which has become a hotbed for discoveries tied to the ancient Roman and early Christian worlds.

This summer, archaeologists unveiled a rare 1,700-year-old Aramaic inscription at a temple in Turkey, offering new evidence of Christianity's rise over the mysterious cult Mithraism.

Last fall, excavators uncovered a Roman military hospital that was later converted into a Christian sanctuary in the ancient Turkish city of Kaunos.

item.title: Salman Rushdie attacker convicted of federal terrorism charges, motivated by Iranian fatwa
item.description: Hadi Matar faces life in prison after a federal jury convicted him of terrorism charges related to his knife attack on Salman Rushdie in 2022.
item.content:encoded:
The man who stabbed Salman Rushdie more than a dozen times on stage at an event in western New York was found guilty Wednesday of attempting to carry out a fatwa issued by Iran’s government against the award-winning British author more than 30 years earlier.

Hadi Matar, 28, is already serving a 25-year sentence after he was convicted last year in state court of attempted murder for the 2022 knife attack that left Rushdie blind in one eye and with nerve damage.

On Wednesday, a federal jury in Buffalo took less than two hours to convict Matar of all three charges — attempting to provide material support to the Iran-backed Hezbollah terrorist group, committing an act of terrorism that transcended national boundaries, and providing material support to terrorists, Reuters reported.

He now faces a maximum of life in prison and is set to be sentenced on November 3.

A HEZBOLLAH VETERAN IS HUNTING JEWS IN US COURTS — WE JUST NAMED HIM TO THE DOJ

Federal prosecutors argued that Matar had been enraged by Rushdie's 1988 novel "The Satanic Verses," which portrayed a fictionalized version of Muhammad that many Muslims saw as blasphemous.

A year later, Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini issued a fatwa, or a religious edict, urging Muslims across the world to kill Rushdie. Iran's government later backed away from the fatwa, only for Khomeini's successor, Ali Khamenei, to reaffirm it in 2017, Reuters reported, citing the U.S. Attorney's Office.

Prosecutors said Matar, who was born in the U.S. but has Lebanese citizenship, spent more than a year studying the fatwa before attempting to fulfill it. He had also turned to Islam after a visit to the Middle East years before the eventual attack.

On August 12, 2022, Rushdie was speaking at the Chautauqua Institution in Mayville, New York, when Matar rushed onstage and repeatedly stabbed the Indian-born author in the head, neck, torso and left hand.

MOJTABA KHAMENEI USING ‘BIN LADEN TEMPLATE’ TO SURVIVE, LEARNED FROM ABBOTTABAD: ANALYST

Matar's federal trial weighed whether he had committed an act of terrorism by attacking Rushdie.

Although prosecutors acknowledged that Matar never contacted anyone in Hezbollah, they argued that without the fatwa, he never would have been motivated to try to kill Rushdie, The New York Times reported.

Prosecutors presented Matar's notes to the jury, which referenced "Jihad" and the "need to kill him ASAP," according to the Times.

Matar's defense attorney, Nathaniel L. Barone II, argued that his client acted independently and was not being controlled by Hezbollah.

AMERICAN ‘JIHAD’ FUELED BY 'RISKY SOURCE' INSIDE US BORDERS, WARNS NATIONAL SECURITY EXPERT

Prosecutors countered by showing evidence of Matar's devotion to Hezbollah, which included a photo of him wearing a Hezbollah shirt while making a salute, an essay he wrote that praised the terrorist group and a video he created using remarks from a former leader of Hezbollah, the Times reported.

Timothy Lynch, a federal prosecutor, said in his closing statement that Matar "wanted to be forever revered as a Hezbollah martyr," according to the Times.

Rushdie, who testified at the trial, has previously described the attack as something that took him back to the "distant past," when he spent a decade in hiding after the fatwa was issued.

"I saw the man in black running towards me, down the right-hand side of the seating area: black clothes, black face mask – he was coming in hard and low, a squat missile," Rushdie told "60 Minutes" host Anderson Cooper in April 2024. "I confess, I had sometimes imagined my assassin rising up in some public forum or other and coming for me in this way."

item.title: NATO member scrambles fighter jets as Russian attack on Ukraine kills 8
item.description: Poland scrambled fighter jets after a suspected Russian Kh-101 missile entered its airspace during a massive barrage of over 70 missiles and 280 drones.
item.content:encoded:
Poland, the closest NATO member to the Ukraine-Russia war, scrambled fighter jets and placed its air defenses on high alert early Thursday as Russia launched more than 70 missiles and roughly 280 drones across Ukraine, killing at least eight and wounding dozens from Kyiv to the western city of Lviv.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, just returning from this week's U.S. visit with President Donald Trump and the funeral of late Sen. Lindsey Graham, R-S.C., said the barrage exposed a critical shortage of Western-supplied interceptors, particularly against ballistic missiles.

"The protection of people’s lives depends directly on their willingness" to provide Ukraine with air-defense missiles, Zelenskyy said of Kyiv’s allies.

Hours later Thursday morning, the European Union disbursed $4 billion to Ukraine to finance the procurement of more drones, missiles, air defense and fighter jets, according to the European Commission.

RUSSIA LAUNCHES BALLISTIC MISSILE ATTACK ON KYIV HOURS AFTER ZELENSKYY WARNS OF MAJOR STRIKE

The disbursement is part of a more than $100 billion loan approved by the EU earlier this year and follows the roughly $3.5 billion installment on June 25 and $4.5 billion on June 30.

Polish forces detected an unidentified object moving west through the country’s airspace shortly before 4 a.m. An F-16 was dispatched to intercept it, but the object disappeared from radar minutes later. Authorities subsequently found a crater about 33 feet wide and scattered debris in farmland near Tarnawa-Kolonia, about 1.2 miles from the closest buildings.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said initial evidence indicated the object was a Russian Kh-101 missile, although investigators were still working to confirm its type and origin.

THE TWO MOST IMPORTANT AMERICAN WEAPONS SYSTEMS NATO IS EAGER TO HAVE

"All the indications are that it was a Russian Kh-101," Tusk said, adding that Polish forces were prepared to shoot it down if it had continued flying toward a populated area.

He added the U.S. is interested in joining the investigation, which has initially determined the missile was not intended for Poland territory. The fate of the Ukraine-Russian war might be decided within the next 100 days, Tusk told reporters.

The threat to a NATO ally is a new frontier in the long-running war and comes after Zelenskyy pressed senators to advance Graham's sweeping sanctions package. Also, Trump and Zelenskyy discussed U.S. licenses allowing Ukraine to produce Patriot interceptors, along with other defense cooperation and efforts to revive stalled diplomacy with Moscow.

Six people, including two girls ages 5 and 12, were killed when a Russian Iskander-M ballistic missile struck a private home housing a large family near Kryvyi Rih, according to local officials. Seven others were reported killed in Kyiv and elsewhere in the Dnipropetrovsk and Poltava regions as the casualty count rose during rescue operations.

'WRITTEN IN OUR DNA': POLISH PILOTS WHO REMEMBER SOVIET RULE PREPARE FOR AMERICA'S MOST LETHAL FIGHTER JET

"A dark night," Oleksandr Vilkul, the head of Kryvyi Rih’s defense council, wrote on Telegram. Eight people were wounded in the strike on the home.

The person killed in Kyiv was a 31-year-old man, while two others were wounded, according to Ukrainian police. Russian strikes damaged residential buildings, vehicles, storage facilities, a market and a garage complex in the capital, where air raid warnings lasted more than five hours and thousands of residents sheltered in subway stations.

In Lviv, about 40 miles from the Polish border, emergency crews searched damaged apartment buildings for people trapped beneath concrete and debris. Thirty people, including children, were reported injured. More than 20 residential buildings, a school and two kindergartens were damaged, officials said.

"I was terrified watching the rescuers go beneath those concrete slabs," one Lviv resident told Reuters as crews pulled a boy from a damaged building.

Ukraine’s air force said its defenses intercepted 55 missiles and 265 drones. But only one of nine ballistic missiles was shot down, while 11 missiles and 17 drones struck targets at 20 locations.

The U.S.-made Patriot is the only system currently in Ukraine’s arsenal capable of reliably intercepting Russian ballistic missiles, which travel at several times the speed of sound. Zelenskyy has repeatedly warned that Patriot interceptors are arriving too slowly and in insufficient numbers.

During his Tuesday meeting with Trump, Zelenskyy said the leaders discussed licenses for Patriot interceptor production in Ukraine. He also met with Lockheed Martin executives and told senators that domestic production would be a long-term solution but would not address Ukraine’s immediate shortage of missiles. European countries have offered to pay for additional U.S.-made interceptors.

Zelenskyy’s Washington visit coincided with Senate consideration of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, named for the longtime defense hawk and outspoken Ukraine supporter who died unexpectedly earlier this month.

The Senate voted 86-12 Tuesday to clear an initial procedural hurdle and voted 84-12 Wednesday to formally proceed with the legislation. Additional votes were still required before final passage.

The package would impose sanctions on Russian officials, oligarchs, financial institutions, energy projects and vessels accused of helping Moscow evade existing restrictions. It would also authorize tariffs of up to 100% on goods from the five largest purchasers of Russian oil and natural gas and the leading countries facilitating sanctions evasion.

Graham negotiated the revised package with the White House shortly before his death. The legislation also includes an extension of sanctions targeting Iran’s energy and weapons sectors, a provision sought by the Trump administration.

Zelenskyy met with a bipartisan group of senators before the procedural votes and called the legislation an important signal to Russia, Europe and the Ukrainian people. He watched the Senate vote from the chamber’s gallery after attending Graham’s funeral at Washington National Cathedral.

Reuters and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Hawley moves to close federal cash prize loopholes after Fauci 'got rich while millions of people died'
item.description: Josh Hawley's new bill targets federal employees accepting cash prizes after accusing Anthony Fauci of using NIH staff to solicit over $1 million in awards.
item.content:encoded:

"No federal bureaucrat should accept cash prizes while on the job. That’s why I’m introducing legislation to bar federal employees from accepting cash prizes or soliciting awards. Fauci got rich while millions of people died. It can never happen again," Hawley told Fox News Digital in a statement.

TOP 5 MOMENTS FROM FAUCI'S HEARING: PAUL BOOTS LAWYER, MORENO ERUPTS AS CONTEMPT VOTE LOOMS

Hawley cited public records showing that Fauci, while director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), used employees to solicit at least eight cash awards for himself, with one award check alone totaling $900,000.

The new legislation would block federal employees from receiving rewards for medicine and research as well as block employees from soliciting such rewards. It would also strengthen existing federal regulations that block National Institutes of Health officials from using their or a subordinate's official duty time to solicit rewards.

The bill comes after Hawley thrashed Fauci during a Wednesday hearing with the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, during which Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment over 100 times.

RAND PAUL SEEKS CONTEMPT CHARGES AFTER FAUCI INVOKES FIFTH AMENDMENT MORE THAN 100 TIMES

"But I think I know why you're doing it," Hawley said of Fauci's refusal to testify. "It's because you don't want to answer questions. It's because you did all kinds of terrible things. It's because during the pandemic, you got rich… while people were dying."

"You were using federal employees with taxpayer money to apply for and solicit cash prizes for you personally, cash prizes totaling over $1 million," Hawley said. "You did all of that during the pandemic, didn't you?"

Rather than respond to Hawley's questions, Fauci repeatedly said, "On the advice of counsel, I respectfully decline to answer based upon my rights under the Fifth Amendment to the Constitution."

FAUCI'S NEWLY RELEASED COVID DIARIES REVEAL BIZARRE FIXATION ON FAME AS PANDEMIC DEATHS MOUNTED

Hawley then pointed to what he described as internal emails from Fauci's staff, including one from former chief of staff Greg Folkers discussing a nomination for the Dan David Prize. According to Hawley, the email asked federal employees to bolster the COVID-19 section of Fauci's nomination by providing language detailing his pandemic response.

"We're working on this nomination for the Dan David Award for Fauci," Hawley read from the email. "We need to beef up the COVID part."

Hawley said the Dan David Award carried a $900,000 cash prize and claimed Fauci used federal employees to help obtain it. He further accused Fauci of using government staff and resources to pursue at least eight additional cash awards, including honors from the Partnership for Public Service, the Adelson Prize, the Smithsonian Institution, the National Academy of Medicine and the CDC Foundation.

item.title: WNBA suddenly wants to stick to basketball after years of making politics part of the product
item.description: The WNBA spent years integrating progressive activism into its product, but now its media wants to refocus on basketball after conservative voices arrived.
item.content:encoded:
The WNBA media suddenly wants everyone to stick to basketball.

Well, some members of the WNBA media do. Just not until they’ve decided which players are allowed to speak and which answers are acceptable.

The contradiction was on full display Tuesday night in Seattle, where Storm center Stefanie Dolson arrived for a game against the Indiana Fever wearing a shirt that read, "Trans rights are human rights."

Nobody needed help connecting those dots. Dolson wore the shirt one week after Fever guard Sophie Cunningham publicly opposed allowing biological males to compete in women’s sports.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM RALLY ROCKS WNBA GAME AS 'SAVE WOMEN'S SPORTS' ACTIVISTS FACE COUNTERPROTEST

The Storm then promoted Dolson’s shirt on its official social media accounts, adding three speaking-head emojis to make sure no one missed the message.

After the game, a credentialed member of the WNBA media attempted to question Fever coach Stephanie White about a pregame demonstration outside the arena supporting Cunningham’s position.

Except the "reporter" didn’t frame it as a demonstration supporting women’s sports. She called it an "anti-trans rally" and said Cunningham’s comments had "ignited right-wing and anti-trans supporters."

That’s not how you phrase a question when you’re genuinely interested in hearing the answer. It’s a political statement with a question mark tacked onto the end.

That’s not journalism. It’s activism with a credential.

An Indiana Fever public relations representative eventually interrupted, explained that neither Cunningham nor the organization had anything to do with the demonstration and said the team was focused on winning basketball games.

"Any more basketball questions?" the spokesperson asked.

In that particular moment, it was a fair response.

My colleague Jackson Thompson has the full story on what happened in Seattle. But Tuesday night was really just the latest example of a much larger trend surrounding the WNBA.

The people who spent years celebrating politics as an integral part of women’s basketball suddenly want to recenter the conversation on basketball.

Funny how that works.

Former WNBA player and current ESPN analyst Chiney Ogwumike delivered that message during a recent appearance on "First Take," one of ESPN's most prominent daily shows. So, this wasn’t a throwaway comment on a WNBA-centered podcast with a tiny audience. Ogwumike was speaking on one of the biggest platforms in sports media.

She said it was "time to reset the conversation" around Clark and the WNBA.

"This conversation has reached levels that stray so far away from the sport," she said. "And I feel like it is our responsibility now to recenter it."

She argued that ESPN’s programs "have a choice" about which stories they give airtime and said the focus should be on the "beautiful basketball" being played during the league’s 30th season.

Ogwumike is right about one thing: ESPN programs have a choice about which stories and narratives are presented to the audience.

The problem is that the network spent years using that power to promote the WNBA’s progressive politics. Ogwumike regularly helped it do so.

CHINEY OGWUMIKE'S DEFENSE OF ALYSSA THOMAS REINFORCED EVERYTHING CRITICS SAY ABOUT THE WNBA MEDIA

In 2020, Ogwumike went on ESPN to defend athletes using their platforms to advance political and social causes.

"The reason why you see athletes leading the charge when it comes to social change is because it’s in our DNA," she said.

Ogwumike also argued that "all lives cannot matter unless Black lives matter equally." Huh, that's interesting.

In 2020, Ogwumike was all for athletes "using their platforms" to advance left-wing and progressive causes. She didn't tell players to stick to basketball. In fact, she presented activism as a natural extension of professional athletics.

A year later, Ogwumike served as an executive producer of ESPN’s "144," a documentary about the 2020 WNBA season that prominently celebrated the league’s social activism and political organizing.

Ogwumike acknowledged on "First Take" that she hasn’t "been perfect" in handling the current conversation. That’s fair, and at least she showed some self-awareness.

But let’s be honest about what’s happening here.

Ogwumike doesn’t believe sports and politics should remain separate. She’s made that clear for years. What she really believes is that this particular political discussion has become distracting and damaging.

That’s a reasonable position, but it raises an obvious question: Where was all this concern about recentering the conversation when the WNBA’s politics flowed exclusively in a progressive direction?

ESPN didn’t spend years reluctantly covering political activism that players forced onto its airwaves. The network celebrated that activism as one of the WNBA’s defining qualities. Now Ogwumike is using ESPN’s signature show to argue that ESPN should become more selective about what it amplifies.

Apparently, editorial restraint became important only after the political conversation escaped the boundaries ESPN preferred.

Then there’s Angel Reese.

During Toronto’s July 17 game against Atlanta, Tempo coach Sandy Brondello complained that Reese was being treated like a "protected species" by the officials.

Brondello is Australian, where the phrase is commonly used in sports to describe a player who receives favorable treatment from referees. But Reese took offense, posted the comment on social media, tagged Brondello, added a clown emoji and wrote, "ARE WE SURPRISED?!"

The situation quickly became a national controversy about race and discrimination, largely because Reese deliberately framed it that way. Brondello apologized, explained what she meant and received a one-game suspension from the WNBA.

Reese thanked the league for taking action and said she was grateful everyone could now "move on from the situation and just play winning basketball."

Notice a pattern?

Reese didn’t object when an overheard complaint about officiating became a cultural controversy. She publicly amplified it and made sure an officiating complaint was viewed through a racial lens.

Once the league accepted Reese’s interpretation and suspended the coach, though, it was time to stop talking and get back to basketball.

That’s increasingly what "get back to basketball" appears to mean around the WNBA.

First, arrive at the approved conclusion. Then end the conversation.

ESPN also published a lengthy All-Star Weekend feature lamenting how controversy had swallowed the league. The story quoted a Chicago Sky season-ticket holder saying, "politics has killed my hobby," and ended with another fan wishing everyone could "get back to the game."

To give a quick peek behind the curtain, reporters don’t select quotes like those by accident. The writer used two fans to reinforce the idea that people around the WNBA are exhausted by politics and desperate to get back to basketball. Whether that sentiment is actually representative of the league’s fans is another question.

Yet the same story acknowledged the WNBA’s long relationship with Democratic politicians and declared that the WNBA is never completely devoid of politics.

Well, which is it?

Is politics an essential part of the WNBA’s identity, or is it an unfortunate distraction from basketball?

The answer seems to depend entirely on who’s doing the talking.

Politics didn’t suddenly invade the WNBA because Caitlin Clark became famous or because Sophie Cunningham expressed an opinion shared by the majority of Americans.

The league made a conscious decision to integrate political and social activism into its product.

The WNBA launched an official Pride initiative in 2014. Two years later, the NBA and WNBA became the first professional sports leagues to march and enter a float in New York City’s Pride parade.

In 2016, Lynx players wore shirts referencing Philando Castile, Alton Sterling and Black Lives Matter. Soon after, players from the Indiana Fever, New York Liberty and Phoenix Mercury wore similar shirts, prompting the league to fine those teams and players before rescinding the penalties following backlash and promising to work with the union on player expression.

Then came the 2020 season.

The WNBA and its players’ union launched the Justice Movement and created a Social Justice Council. The league placed Black Lives Matter on its courts, honored Breonna Taylor on player uniforms and said the council would drive conversations about race, voting rights, LGBTQ advocacy and gun control.

This wasn’t a handful of individual players expressing their personal opinions.

It was an official league initiative built directly into the season. The council wasn’t limited to broad appeals for fairness or equality, either. It entered specific policy debates, including gun control.

Players then moved beyond social advocacy and entered a partisan election. WNBA players across the league wore "Vote Warnock" shirts in support of Democratic Senate candidate Raphael Warnock, who was challenging Republican Sen. Kelly Loeffler, then a co-owner of the Atlanta Dream.

Players are free to advocate for political candidates. But when they use nationally televised WNBA games to do it, they can’t later pretend outsiders were responsible for dragging politics into women’s basketball.

Once these players endorsed a political candidate inside WNBA arenas, the argument that politics had no place in women’s basketball was over (if it wasn't already).

The league wasn’t shy about any of this.

In 2024, the WNBA used its Commissioner’s Cup to promote civic engagement and "reproductive health" advocacy.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SPEAKS OUT TO PROTECT GIRLS AS WNBA ALL-STAR INITIATIVE BACKS ‘GENDER-EXPANSIVE’ GROUP

Bethany Donaphin, then the WNBA’s head of league operations, called it "the most progressive league in professional sports."

"So really, why wouldn’t we use one of our marquee league events to address important social issues?" she asked.

Fine.

But the WNBA can’t use its marquee events to advance progressive causes, celebrate players for influencing elections and market activism as a central part of the league’s identity, then become offended when conservatives, Republicans or players with dissenting opinions enter the conversation.

The league told everyone politics belonged in the WNBA.

It was telling a half-truth. What it really meant, as we're seeing now, was that progressive politics belong in the WNBA.

There's an important distinction to make.

Some WNBA players have dealt with harassment on social media. That’s wrong, although it’s hardly unique to them.

Online trolling is bad. Please take a moment to applaud my bravery for saying that.

OK, now we can continue.

Just because online trolling exists doesn’t make every criticism of the WNBA racist, every political disagreement, harassment or every question from Congress a threat.

The league’s defenders constantly lump those things together because it’s easier than answering legitimate criticism. It allows them to say that anyone who challenges the WNBA’s preferred narrative should be dismissed as a hateful bigot.

Sorry, but it doesn’t work that way.

Caitlin Clark brought millions of new viewers to the WNBA. Those viewers don’t all share the politics that dominated the league and its media coverage before she arrived.

Conservative media started paying attention, Republican lawmakers began asking questions and Sophie Cunningham challenged progressive orthodoxy from inside the league.

In other words, the WNBA’s political conversation became more diverse.

Suddenly, the league that never stops preaching about diversity wasn't so excited about having a more politically diverse fan base.

The league’s own website still invites fans to learn how the WNBA is "#MORETHAN basketball."

Great. Be more than basketball.

But the WNBA and its media supporters can’t spend years celebrating that identity, then demand "basketball questions" because someone from the other side finally got a word in.

Drop Site News did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

item.title: Trump accused China of an 'election security nightmare' but then undercut his own warning
item.description: Trump said China's voter file collection happened "a long time ago" and suggested both nations spy on each other as Xi Jinping's September visit proceeds.
item.content:encoded:
Less than two weeks after accusing China of carrying out an "unprecedented election security nightmare," President Donald Trump has not changed his posture toward Beijing and is moving ahead with plans to host Chinese President Xi Jinping in September.

"This data loss presents an unprecedented election security nightmare," Trump said in a July 16 address. "The intelligence even shows that China assigned a data exploitation unit specifically to this new project."

Intelligence officials, he said, "worked to actively suppress and downplay information about the extent of China’s sinister election meddling."

TRUMP’S UPBEAT CHINA MESSAGE COLLIDES WITH DEEPENING BEIJING RIVALRY

Trump did not claim China changed votes or altered election results. Instead, he argued Beijing engaged in an influence campaign aimed at shaping U.S. public perceptions.

But within days of the address, Trump undercut the urgency of his own warning. Asked whether China would face consequences, he said the alleged activity "took place a long time ago" and suggested it reflected the broader intelligence rivalry between the two countries.

"They do things, and we do things to them," Trump said July 21 in remarks to reporters. "I’ll be honest, we do things to them, too. It’s not a one-way street."

So far, the fallout has been directed almost entirely inward. Trump ordered investigations into U.S. officials who handled the intelligence, while his trade and diplomatic engagement with Beijing has continued largely unchanged.

Trump’s posture toward TikTok has undergone a similar shift. He sought to ban the platform during his first term over national-security concerns tied to its Chinese ownership but joined it during the 2024 campaign. Five days after Trump’s address, most Cabinet members launched official accounts after the Justice Department cleared federal employees to use TikTok under its new U.S.-controlled ownership.

It also remains unclear when Trump first learned of the intelligence or whether he knew about it before traveling to Beijing in May. A White House official confirmed Xi's Sept. 24 visit will proceed but did not answer questions about when Trump was briefed or whether anyone accused of withholding the intelligence remains in government.

The Chinese embassy could not immediately be reached for comment on the planned visit.

Newly declassified records released by the administration provide fresh details about China’s alleged collection and analysis of American voter information and reveal an internal intelligence debate over whether Beijing’s broader activities amounted to election interference. But the documents also establish less than some of Trump’s rhetoric appeared to suggest.

CHINA DISMISSES TRUMP ELECTION INTERFERENCE ACCUSATIONS AS 'ENTIRELY FABRICATED,' THREATENS COUNTERMEASURES

During the July 16 address, Trump said China had acquired 220 million U.S. voter files containing names, addresses, phone numbers and political affiliations. He said Beijing assigned a unit to exploit the information which had the potential to use it to register voters or engage in other "nefarious activities."

Trump called the findings "stunning" and the broader vulnerabilities "a cyber threat aimed at the very heart of our democracy."

The president accused intelligence officials of working to "actively suppress and downplay" China’s "sinister election meddling." He cited an internal message saying officials had "deliberately massaged" a pending President’s Daily Brief and another in which an FBI official described "running a shadow government."

'SHADOW GOVERNMENT': TRUMP CLAIMS INTEL COMMUNITY BRAGGED ABOUT HIDING CHINESE MEDDLING

Trump directed the Justice Department, FBI, CIA and Office of the Director of National Intelligence to investigate. He said those responsible should be fired and potentially prosecuted.

The roughly 270 pages of released records show that Chinese entities amassed and analyzed large quantities of American voter information.

The figure at the center of Trump’s announcement appears to come from a record showing that a Chinese entity possessed an unspecified dataset containing approximately 204.8 million American voter records. The document does not identify its source or explain how it was obtained.

Other records describe China analyzing registration information from 18 states and a Chinese actor downloading publicly available historical voter information from six states. The documents do not show that China altered voter rolls, changed ballots or penetrated vote-counting systems.

The documents also include a raw FBI report alleging that China planned to manufacture fraudulent U.S. driver’s licenses that could be used to cast mail ballots for Joe Biden. The allegation came from a single uncorroborated source, and the report was recalled the day it was distributed and never reissued.

There was no evidence that any fraudulent votes were actually cast.

Emily Harding, director of the Intelligence, National Security, and Technology Program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, wrote that China "likely gained little advantage" from voter records that were largely publicly available or available for purchase.

Harding wrote that the internal exchanges showed "an honest, and valuable, analytical debate" rather than a cover-up. She noted that the recalled FBI report relied on unreliable third-hand information and said references to the election were removed from one briefing so a specialized election-security team could address the issue.

Trump did not explain which American activities he considered comparable to China’s collection and analysis of voter information.

There is some public record behind Trump’s suggestion that the intelligence competition runs both ways — but China does not hold free national elections.

Trump authorized the CIA in 2019 to conduct a covert influence campaign against China, Reuters reported in 2024. According to three former U.S. officials, operatives used false online identities to circulate damaging but fact-based information about Xi’s government and attempt to shape public opinion inside China.

The CIA declined to confirm the program. Documents leaked by former National Security Agency contractor Edward Snowden also showed the National Security Agency penetrating Chinese networks, including the systems of telecommunications giant Huawei.

Trump expressed a similar view during his May visit to Beijing, although he was speaking then about Chinese espionage more broadly.

"They spy on us," Trump told Fox News host Sean Hannity during the trip. "We spy on them too, I guess."

Trump otherwise used the visit to promote closer economic ties. He traveled with leading American executives, called Xi a "great leader" and said it was an "honor" to be his friend.

The White House later announced that the two countries had agreed to establish boards of trade and investment. China also committed to purchase 200 Boeing aircraft and at least $17 billion in American agricultural products annually through 2028, according to the administration.

Preparations for Xi’s visit continued after Trump’s address.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi July 22 to lay the groundwork for what he called a "very positive" visit but said Trump’s election allegations were not discussed. Rubio added that it would be "reckless and irresponsible" for the two powers not to maintain a relationship.

China has denied interfering in the 2020 election. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian called the allegations "entirely fabricated" and urged the United States to stop using China as an election issue.

item.title: Daily eating habit linked to better brain health in older adults, new research suggests
item.description: A six-month trial found that older women who ate within eight to nine hours daily showed cognitive improvements beyond what weight loss alone provided.
item.content:encoded:
Eating within a shorter daily window could help support brain health as people age, according to new research.

Preliminary findings presented at NUTRITION 2026 — the American Society for Nutrition’s annual meeting in Maryland — suggests that older women who ate within eight to nine hours per day saw slight cognitive improvement compared to those who spread their meals over about 12 hours each day.

The small six-month trial included 47 postmenopausal obese or overweight women aged 50 to 79. They were each advised to reduce their daily food intake by about 500 calories.

INTERMITTENT FASTING'S REAL BENEFIT MAY COME AFTER YOU START EATING AGAIN

The participants were divided into two groups. One ate in a time-restricted window within an average of 8.2 hours, usually from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. The other group ate across a 12.3-hour window, according to a news release.

Both groups lost about 15 pounds over six months, but those in the shorter eating-window group performed better on cognitive tests measuring spatial planning and problem-solving.

The shorter-window group also showed fewer errors on memory and learning tests, but no meaningful differences in reaction time or multi-tasking ability.

PEOPLE LOST WEIGHT WHILE EATING SIGNIFICANTLY MORE FOOD — HERE'S THE SECRET

"These outcomes suggest a better ability to remember information during everyday tasks and reduce mistakes related to memory, attention and problem-solving," lead researcher Sue Shapses, Ph.D., a professor at Rutgers University and Rutgers-RWJ Medical Center, said in a press release. "Reductions in the eating window predicted greater improvements."

Although the pilot study included only a small number of participants, the researchers believe that time-restricted eating may support brain health by regulating circadian rhythm, reducing inflammation and improving metabolic health.

Losing weight alone can help "ward off some of the aging-related cognitive decline," according to Shapses.

"And these data suggest there may be additional benefits if you stop eating four hours prior to going to sleep and reduce food intake to eight to nine hours per day, compared to the usual eating window of 12 hours per day."

Women, as well as adults who are overweight or obese, tend to face a higher likelihood of developing Alzheimer’s disease and other forms of dementia as they age, according to the researchers.

Lauri Wright, Ph.D., director of nutrition programs and associate professor at the USF College of Public Health, who was not involved in this research, reflected on these findings in an interview with Fox News Digital.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"This is an interesting study because it suggests that when we eat may matter in addition to what and how much we eat," she said. "That suggests meal timing itself may have played a role, not just weight loss."

"The results are promising, but we need larger, longer studies before recommending time-restricted eating specifically to improve brain health."

Experts are still learning about how intermittent fasting affects the brain, although "several biological mechanisms are being considered," Wright noted.

"Giving the body a longer overnight break from eating may improve insulin sensitivity, reduce chronic inflammation, support healthy circadian rhythms and allow cells more time for repair and maintenance," she said. "Those processes are all linked to healthy brain aging."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

From a practical standpoint, eating within a shorter daily window often leads people to consume fewer calories, which can promote weight loss, according to New York-based certified holistic nutritionist Robin DeCicco.

"We know that maintaining a healthy weight helps with virtually everything," she told Fox News Digital. "Eating within a restricted window helps people cut calories."

"When you fast or... have periods of time where you're not just eating throughout the whole day, it does help to lower markers of inflammation and certain sources of oxidative stress."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Many people have reported "feeling better" when fasting, DeCicco noted — especially those who have inflammatory conditions, which can include neurological disorders like Alzheimer’s and dementia.

"When you're fasting, you're giving your organs a chance to rest, you're giving the digestive system a chance to ‘rest and digest,’" she added.

Intermittent fasting isn’t the only way to support cognitive health, Wright countered.

"Regular physical activity, adequate sleep, controlling blood pressure and blood sugar, avoiding smoking, maintaining social connections and following an overall healthy dietary pattern, such as the Mediterranean diet, have much stronger evidence for protecting cognitive function over time," she said. "Think of meal timing as one potential piece of the puzzle rather than a magic bullet."

Intermittent fasting "isn’t appropriate for everyone," Wright warned, adding that she would advise against it for children and teens, pregnant or breastfeeding women, anyone with a history of an eating disorder, and people with diabetes who are taking insulin.

DeCicco agreed that fasting should be recommended and monitored by a medical professional, especially for those who take certain medications or have certain conditions.

item.title: Trump tells foreign students: Overstay your visa, face the consequences
item.description: Foreign students dragging out degrees while working illegally or filing frivolous asylum claims face new accountability under a final administrative rule.
item.content:encoded:
Amid all the noise in Washington and simultaneous lack of legislation coming out of Congress, there have been some quiet wins for accountability in our visa system.

One recent win is an administrative final rule that requires foreign students to comply with their visas. Administrative rules govern how the government implements the law in practice.

Most foreign students who qualify get an F-1 visa, which allows them to study at the undergraduate or graduate level. Some get a J-1, which is for international exchange visitors.

RUBIO PUSHES BACK ON INDIA'S CONCERNS OVER US VISA CURBS, SAYS POLICY MUST BE 'AMERICA FIRST' UNDER TRUMP

When student visa holders arrive here, they are given permission to enter under what’s called "duration of status." That means that as long as they are full-time students, they can stay.

An earlier rule allows students, while still on their student visas, to work in "Optional Practical Training" for a year, with another two years if they have STEM degrees. The definition of STEM is 16 pages long and generous. Because foreigners on OPT are working using their student visa (remember – "duration of status") their employers are not required to pay into Social Security and Medicare. That’s a discount of up to 15% for hiring foreign workers instead of Americans.

"Duration of status" combined with OPT incentivizes marginal students not to complete their degrees in due course and, as they originally claimed they would, go home.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION ORDERS GREEN CARD APPLICANTS TO LEAVE THE US, APPLY FROM THEIR HOME COUNTRIES

The education-migration complex is desperate to keep the foreign student gravy train on the rails. They make the new rule seem as if it is cutting off opportunity. Quite the opposite: it’s about asking for responsibility.

It’s not hard to complete a bachelor’s degree in four years, especially for foreign students. Americans can apply to college knowing they’ll need to work or apply for aid and grants. Foreigners, meanwhile, are required to show consular officers in their visa interview that they can afford the entire course of study, including tuition, lodging and incidental costs. They are not, in theory, supposed to work.

If they decide to earn a master’s after their bachelor's, or even a Ph.D., the new rule just means they have to go home, apply for a new visa, and show the consular officer they are credible students, can afford the entire course of study and intend to return home when done.

TRUMP PUTS ASYLUM LAWYERS ‘ON NOTICE’ WITH NEW FRONT IN WAR ON FRAUD

That’s what is really freaking out the edu-crats. Many foreign students intend to stay in the U.S. Some never go to school at all; these get dropped from the Student and Exchange Visitor Information System (SEVIS) maintained by DHS. They should then be deported, but many make frivolous asylum claims to remain.

Others do go to school, but drag it out over many years, taking minimal classes to maintain status while working, often illegally. Schools don’t mind, as long as the fees keep coming.

But we should mind. America doesn’t need to import this type of low-motivation student.

What America needs even less are students who come here pre-programmed with hostility to the United States, Western civilization and capitalism, who spend their time protesting on campus.

Some foreign students on campuses across the United States have been here for years, spending far too much time and energy protesting Israel, capitalism, ICE and Western civilization instead of hitting the books and getting a degree. These permanent students aren’t adding to our national prosperity, security or unity.

America wants students who come, study and finish their degrees. The left will tell you that foreign students are all the best of the best. Not so. As a consular officer, I did thousands of student visa applications in Africa, Asia and Europe. I’ve seen everything from applicants with full scholarships at MIT and Harvard to those wanting to study English at a community college near their uncle, who just happens to own a motel or gas station.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

America welcomes legitimate students. We will always have room for the most talented and entrepreneurial to stay. But our universities are not there to facilitate mass economic migration.

The unemployment rate for recent American college graduates is 5.7%, higher than the national average. They need our support, not millions of foreign graduates to compete with.

The new rule on student visas is timely and welcome. Future presidents would be wise to keep it instead of caving to the education and migration lobby.
